concepts.def: The study of structures that are 1–100 nm in size, of the order of a few hundred atoms. Such structures are far bigger than a single atom but far too small to be seen with a light microscope.
A particle in the 1–100 nm size range. Nanoparticles are smaller than fine particles (PM2.5) and contain of the order of a few hundred atoms.
Particles with diameters between 100 and 2500 nm (1 x 10⁻⁷ m and 2.5 x 10⁻⁶ m). They are larger than nanoparticles and smaller than coarse particles.
Particles with diameters between 1 x 10⁻⁵ m and 2.5 x 10⁻⁶ m. Coarse particles are often referred to as dust.
One thousand-millionth of a metre, 1 x 10⁻⁹ m. A nanometre is one thousand times smaller than a micrometre, so 2.5 x 10⁻⁶ m is the same length as 2500 nm.
The total surface area of an object divided by its volume. For a cube of side l it is 6l² ÷ l³, which equals 6 ÷ l, so the ratio rises as the cube gets smaller.
As the side of cube decreases by a factor of 10 the surface area to volume ratio increases by a factor of 10.
The same substance in ordinary, much larger pieces. Its surface area to volume ratio is low, so its properties can differ from those of the identical material as nanoparticles.
The mass of a material needed to do a job. Because nanoparticles expose so much surface, smaller quantities are needed to be effective than for materials with normal particle sizes.
A single atom is roughly 0.1 nm across and small molecules are a fraction of a nanometre wide, so a 1 nm structure is only about ten atoms across and a 100 nm particle is hundreds of atoms across.
Nanoparticles have many applications in medicine, in electronics, in cosmetics and sun creams, as deodorants, and as catalysts. New applications are an important area of research.
A catalyst supplied as nanoparticles rather than as larger lumps or pellets. The very large surface area per gram means a smaller mass produces the same catalytic effect.
Weighing the advantages of a use of nanoparticles against its disadvantages, using only the information given, and reaching a judgement that refers to both sides.
A harm that might follow from using nanoparticles, for example effects on the body or the environment that have not yet been fully tested because the materials are new.

mcqs.q: Which particles have diameters between 1 x 10⁻⁷ m and 2.5 x 10⁻⁶ m?
options: Fine particles, which are known as PM2.5
Coarse particles, often called dust
Nanoparticles, which are 1–100 nm wide
Single atoms and simple molecules
mcqs.explain: 1 x 10⁻⁷ m to 2.5 x 10⁻⁶ m is 100 to 2500 nm, the range the specification gives for fine particles.

mcqs.q: A particle in smoke is measured and found to have a diameter of 5 x 10⁻⁶ m. Which class of particle is it?
options: A nanoparticle, 1 to 100 nm across
A coarse particle, often called dust
A fine particle, one of the PM2.5 class
A single atom, about 0.1 nm wide
mcqs.explain: 5 x 10⁻⁶ m lies between 2.5 x 10⁻⁶ m and 1 x 10⁻⁵ m, the coarse particle range, and coarse particles are often referred to as dust.

mcqs.q: The side of a cube of a solid is decreased by a factor of 10. What happens to its surface area to volume ratio?
options: It decreases by a factor of ten
It increases by one hundred times
It increases by a factor of 10
It stays the same, both fall
mcqs.explain: The ratio for a cube of side l is 6l² ÷ l³ = 6 ÷ l, so dividing the side by 10 multiplies the ratio by 10.

mcqs.q: A cube of side 1 cm has a surface area to volume ratio of 6. What is the ratio for a cube of side 0.1 cm?
options: 6, unchanged by the cutting up
600, a hundred times bigger than 6
0.6, ten times less than before
60, ten times the first cube
mcqs.explain: The ratio is 6 ÷ l, so a side of 0.1 cm gives 6 ÷ 0.1 = 60: as the side falls by 10 the ratio rises by 10.

mcqs.q: Nanoparticles of a metal can behave differently from a lump of the same metal. Why?
options: They are a more reactive element than the metal
They have a much higher surface area to volume ratio
They are built from different atoms than the lump
They each contain fewer than roughly ten atoms
mcqs.explain: The specification attributes the different properties to the high surface area to volume ratio of nanoparticles.

mcqs.q: A sun cream can be made using a metal oxide in bulk form or as nanoparticles of the same oxide. Compared with the bulk form, the mass of the nanoparticle form needed to protect the skin is:
options: larger, since each particle is so very tiny
the same, because the oxide is unchanged
smaller, as far more surface gets exposed
larger, as less surface area is exposed
mcqs.explain: The specification states that smaller quantities are needed to be effective than for materials with normal particle sizes.

mcqs.q: A typical atom has a diameter of about 0.1 nm. Roughly how many atoms would fit across a structure 1 nm wide?
options: About a thousand atoms wide
About one hundred atoms
One atom: 1 nm is one atom
About ten atoms in a row
mcqs.explain: 1 nm ÷ 0.1 nm = 10, so a 1 nm structure is only about ten atoms across.

mcqs.q: A nanoparticle is 20 nm across. A typical atom is about 0.1 nm across. Roughly how many atoms lie along one edge of the nanoparticle?
options: About 20 atoms across
About 200 atoms across
About 2000 atoms across
About 20 000 atoms across
mcqs.explain: 20 nm ÷ 0.1 nm = 200, so the particle is a few hundred atoms across, as the specification says.

mcqs.q: Which list gives only applications of nanoparticles named in the specification?
options: Medicines, fertilisers, road salt, alloys, water pipes
Research laboratories and specialised university work
Medicine, electronics, sun creams, deodorants, catalysts
Electronics, cement, steel making, glass, plastics
mcqs.explain: These are exactly the applications the specification lists for nanoparticles.

mcqs.q: A sun cream made with nanoparticles of a metal oxide is clear on the skin and blocks more ultraviolet light than the bulk form, but its long-term effects on skin cells have not yet been fully tested. Which is the best evaluation?
options: It should be banned, since untested means it is known to be harmful
It should be used, because it blocks the most ultraviolet light
There is nothing to pick, as both creams act in the same way
Better protection and appearance, but long-term effects untested
mcqs.explain: Uses both sides of the information given and reaches a judgement that names the benefit and the uncertainty.

mcqs.q: A factory can buy a catalyst as 5 kg of pellets or as 50 g of nanoparticles that speed the reaction just as much. The nanoparticle form costs more per gram. Which evaluation uses this information best?
options: Much less mass is needed, so a higher price per gram may pay off
Neither wins, since a catalyst cannot change the reaction rate
Nanoparticles are better, since they are used up much more slowly
The pellets are better, because the nanoparticles cost more per gram
mcqs.explain: Weighs the hundredfold smaller mass against the higher unit price, exactly as the information invites.

mcqs.q: Why do scientists say there are possible risks in using nanoparticles?
options: They are on sale already, which proves they are safe
They may enter cells and effects are not known
They are far too small to affect the body's cells
They are used up in reactions, leaving a harmful waste
mcqs.explain: Their size lets them reach places larger particles cannot, and the long-term effects have not been fully tested.
